title: 美国空管技术：部分追溯到二战时期，感恩节高峰边飞边修？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: This Thanksgiving tomorrow in America's Transportation Department reckons this holiday period will be the busiest for air travel in 16 years.
segments.zh: 明天就是感恩节，美国交通部估计这个假期将是16年来航空旅行最繁忙的时期。

segments.en: That's causing concern in some quarters, just weeks after a nationwide ground stop turning attention to America's aging air traffic technology.
segments.zh: 这在一些方面引发了担忧，就在几周前，全国范围内的地面停飞让人们的注意力转向美国老化的空中交通技术。

segments.en: Let's bring in Bloomberg, managing editor for Space and Aviation, better to camel for more.
segments.zh: 让我们请来彭博社太空与航空 managing editor，Better to Camel 了解更多。

segments.en: Benny, we're just talking about cyber risks there linked in with the questions of outdated and old infrastructure.
segments.zh: Benny，我们刚刚谈到网络风险，这与过时老旧的基础设施问题相关。

segments.en: What is the issue with US air traffic technology?
segments.zh: 美国空中交通技术存在什么问题？

segments.en: Well, one of the big issues with the system is that it is so big and so complex and that it's a living, breathing organism that you have to try and fix as you're using it.
segments.zh: 嗯，该系统的一大问题是它如此庞大和复杂，就像一个活生生的有机体，你必须在使用的过程中尝试修复它。

segments.en: Imagine you're changing the tyres on a moving car or you're putting your hands into the spokes of a bicycle wheel, that kind of thing.
segments.zh: 想象一下你在给行驶中的汽车换轮胎，或者把手伸进自行车轮的辐条里，诸如此类。

segments.en: That sort of what we're faced with here that you are trying to operate a system while repairing it and it's a system that has grown over decades in some cases.
segments.zh: 这就是我们面临的情况：你试图在运营一个系统的同时修复它，而这个系统在某些情况下已经发展了几十年。

segments.en: Some of the technology, as we reported in our story for this out today, is decades old.
segments.zh: 正如我们今天发布的报道所述，一些技术已经有几十年的历史了。

segments.en: It sort of goes back to some of it to World War II kind of technology, obviously updated but always sort of added a bit, tweaked a bit here, taken away something there.
segments.zh: 其中一些可以追溯到二战时期的技术，显然已经更新过，但总是这里加一点，那里调整一下，再删掉一些。

segments.en: It's never been sort of a system whereby you can stop the whole thing, repair it, reboot it and that's what they have to deal with.
segments.zh: 从来不存在那种能整体停机、修复、重启的系统，这就是他们必须面对的现实。
